_comment: Illustrative values tuned for gameplay, not engineering data. startupMin: cold start to warm standby (units without syncMin go straight online); syncMin: standby to online; shutdownMin in game minutes; rampPctPerMin and minStablePct in % of unit size; inertiaH in seconds; costPerMWh in NT$ (placeholder marginal cost); standbyCostPerMWh: NT$ per MW of unit size per hour kept warm; co2PerMWh in tonnes; fuel: which fuel-cost group the type counts under; autoRole: what Auto does (follow = adjust output to follow the load; backup = start units when supply is short and stand them down after; hydro = cover shortfalls, pacing the day's water; curtail = run at full output, curtailed only for a surplus nothing else can absorb; storage and demand response have their own rules); unitMW: typical unit size used by the custom mix. capexEURPerKW (capexEURPerKWh and energyLifeYears for battery energy; capexOffshoreEURPerKW for offshore wind) and lifeYears are the technology-data 2030 projections (EUR, 2013 prices) used by the Taiwan PyPSA-Earth model (https://bartonchentw.github.io/pypsa-earth/, data/costs.csv; battery USD converted at 0.7532 EUR/USD); they give the overall system cost range on the setup screen. ammoniaCcgt, geothermal and biomass come from the Taiwan energy model (https://github.com/BartonChenTW/taiwan-energy-model): ammonia turbines take the CCGT investment cost (as in the model) and about NT$5,240/MWh for fuel and O&M (ammonia imported at 80 EUR/MWh, Hampp et al. 2023, at the model's 57% efficiency and NT$36.185/EUR); geothermal 4,220 EUR/kW (the model's IRENA 2023 value) and biomass 2,338 EUR/kW (DIW, via PyPSA); biomass CO2 counts as zero (biogenic), as in the model. costPerMWh and co2PerMWh of nuclear, coal, gas, oil, biomass and geothermal are the model's 2030 values: fuel price / efficiency + variable O&M (EUR/MWh, at NT$36.185/EUR), and fuel CO2 / efficiency (gas 24.57 EUR and 0.198 t, coal 9.55 EUR and 0.336 t, oil 52.91 EUR and 0.257 t, uranium 3.41 EUR, biomass 7.41 EUR per MWh of fuel; efficiencies CCGT 58%, OCGT 41%, coal 35.6%, oil 35%, nuclear 32.6%, biomass 46.8%). Ammonia turbines: 80 EUR/MWh at 57% plus the CCGT O&M. gasCcgtCcs is a gas combined cycle with 95% carbon capture, as in the model (NETL Cost and Performance Baseline Rev. 4a: investment x 2.041, efficiency x 0.885, so 51.3%): gas 24.57 EUR/MWh / 51.3% + the CCGT O&M + 10 EUR per tonne of CO2 stored, and 5% of the CO2 released. h2Ocgt is a gas turbine peaker burning imported hydrogen at 90 EUR/MWh (the model's price) at the OCGT's 41%, plus the OCGT O&M; no CO2. Hydro, demand response and standby costs are still placeholders.
